scope: Private authenticated SH1/SH2 ROMs were copied into isolated temporary directories. No ROM, RAM, PCM, save-state bytes or screenshots are published.
The 18-stage sweep covers the opening 4000 native refreshes per selected stage, not full playthroughs. Native stage transitions may advance beyond the selected starting stage.
Stage selection and remaining-lives preconditions are explicit test-only diagnostics, never distributed core patches. Pause flags and frame diversity verify that the longer tests actually advance.

Each extended sequence watches 10301 native refreshes (2600 through 12900), with no inactive Mark VI list. Inputs begin from stages 1, 5, 7 and 18; two sequences present 26000 frames at double refresh.

Original (M2) video, full PCM and sampled CPU/RAM match the previous core in the tested SH1/SH2 4000-frame sequences. Mark VI comparisons require unchanged full PCM and sampled CPU/RAM while video differs.
SH2 Mark VI changes include the intentional shared left-edge clipping correction; this is not a claim of unchanged enhanced video.
Constructor multiset comparisons do not prove ordering or final pixels. Screenshot review cannot by itself prove absence of temporal flicker.
These gameplay results are from macOS arm64. Release CI separately compiles all desktop targets and runs its public generic-cartridge Windows runtime checks.
